implementerProof.how: Round 2. The implementer's new proof entry claims `block_account` now gives one rule to the three readings of a deployment block's account. I drove it rather than read it: extracted `block_account` out of scripts/e2e/stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh with the repository's own scripts/e2e/lib/script-functions.ts and ran it on four blocks — `{"service_account":"legion-infra-worker"}`, one naming the field at all, `{"service_account":""}` and `{"service_account":null}` — which print legion-infra-worker, default, default and default, so the identity the deployment-pod-block checkpoint builds from it (`system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<account>`) is a real account in every case. Then end to end on the surface the defect showed on: with `pod_block` the empty-account block, `pod_account=$(block_account)` is `default`, and `shape_problems` run on the runtime's own golden operator-route pod with `spec.serviceAccountName` set to `default` prints no serviceAccountName line at all, where last round it printed `serviceAccountName default` and failed the pod-shape checkpoint on a correct pod. My red test is green and untouched: `bun test scripts/e2e/lib/stage4b-pods.test.ts` is 59 pass / 0 fail at this head, against 56 pass / 3 fail at commit 7ca6678fcf18, and `jj diff -r 7ca6678fcf18..5a2b5301780b -- scripts/e2e/lib/stage4b-pods.test.ts` is empty, so the test that pinned the defect is the one that passes. Round 1's verdict on the other five proof entries stands and was re-measured here at this head, not carried over on trust: the loader refusals and `Config OK`, the three live proofs' gate, the A2 greps and the full library suite are all re-run below, and `go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox/... ./internal/config/...` answered `(cached)` for both packages, which is itself the evidence that no Go byte changed between the head I ran it green on (223.396s) and this one.

proof.criterion: Round 1's failure, now fixed: R5 / A2, the LEGION_E2E_POD_FILE lane — the account a deployment's pod block names is read by one rule, an absent `service_account` and an empty one both meaning the namespace's `default`.

proof.command: bun test scripts/e2e/lib/stage4b-pods.test.ts; then, in one bash -c with the two functions sourced: pod_block=<a block holding {"service_account":""}>; pod_account=$(block_account); shape_problems < <the golden root-operator-route pod with spec.serviceAccountName=default>
